Title: Estimates average as-printed and annealed values of one formulation as repeats
Evidence: build/src/estimates.js:201-231 kindOf ignores postProcessing; estimates.js:264 groups by material|formulation|kind and averages ys. G019-01 PLA-GF HDT 0.45: V000350 75.5 (headline) + V000353 114.7 annealed -> one observation 95.1; HDT 1.8 V000349 59.7 + V000352 84 -> 71.85. G068-02 PET-GF HDT 0.45: V001931 81.6 (headline) + V001933 133.7 -> 107.65; HDT 1.8 V001930/V001932. G074-02 PPS-GF: anneal 130 vs 230 C V002071 236.3/V002072 248.9 and V001392 125.8/V002073 219.6 -> 172.7. Consequences in build/reports/validation-report.md: EST-OUTLIER PET-GF hdt045 81.6 expected about 114; conflicts down-weighted for PLA-GF, PET-GF, PPS-GF; the mixed pairs also feed the HDT 1.8->0.45 conversion and the unstated-load bracket back-test (estimates.js:316-320, 648-662). M019 mechanical P/A rows are averaged too (small differences).
SuggestedFix: Give Post-processing a declared state as Moisture condition has one (schema/vocab/post-processing.csv: as-printed | annealed | not-stated, or a typed column), add it to kindOf (" annealed" kind with a documented offset for hdt045, or excluded from hdt045), and include it in the group key. Add a test pinning PET-GF and PLA-GF observation values.

Title: Film specimen values veto estimate screens: PLA stays a candidate for tensile strength >= 140 MPa
Evidence: build/src/compile.js:402-411 impliedBounds excludes only Raw material specimens; app/js/engine/constraints.js:107 lets any bound meeting the requirement veto the screen. M001 PLA tensileStrengthXY bounds include V000039 110.3 MPa and V002179 144.7 MPa, both "Film specimen (ASTM D882)" (estimates.js:176 already excludes film from the model). Engine result: >=70, >=100 and >=140 MPa are not screened (vetoedBy V000039/V002179) although the estimate is 46.9-67.8 MPa plausible. Also V001700 PVB Filament specimen tensile yield bounds M093. No moisture or post-processing filter: a conditioned PA elongation (V001039 216.5 vs dry 9.9) or an annealed HDT at 1.8 MPa (V001932 87.3 vs as-printed 0.45 MPa 81.6) would bound a dry or as-printed headline from below. The same film rows appear in related.intervals (compile.js:456) and get no film reason in related.why (compile.js:428-435).
SuggestedFix: In impliedBounds require a printed or unspecified specimen (exclude /^Film/ and Filament), a dry or not-stated moisture state for elongation (conditioning raises PA strain), and not annealed for HDT; add film to the related.why chain. Add a constraints/database test: no bound from a film, filament, conditioned-elongation or annealed-HDT row.

Title: Estimates merge source-label and XZ directions into XY that compile refuses to call XY
Evidence: build/src/estimates.js:194 DIRECTION_CLASS maps XZ, horizontal-source-label and along-flow to XY (no conversion, no extra spread) and vertical-xz-source-label to Z; build/src/normalize/direction.js:1-3 and Method say a source label "never merges into XY". M093 PVB tensileModulusXY is not published (compile keeps V001705 "Horizontal (source label)" out), yet its estimate is strength this-grade, precision good, centre 1.76 GPa, canScreen true, built from V001705/V001706. Plain XZ (on-edge, loaded in plane) is XY-like, but "Vertical XZ (source label)" is sent to Z: the two XZ spellings get opposite classes.
Repro: node docs/audits/2026-09-15-filtering-estimates-data/pipeline/repro/mapper.mjs (see Direction rows in mapper-table.csv); node -e "const db=require('./dist/db.json');console.log(db.materials.find(m=>m.id==='M093').headline.tensileModulusXY.estimate.evidence)"
SuggestedFix: Give source-label directions their own kinds (e.g. "tensile label") with a documented conversion and spread in estimate-model.json, or class them unk; decide and document XZ once (DECISIONS), and make vertical-xz-source-label consistent with it.

Title: A published mean with a +/- band never passes: 128 of 362 headlines are hard intervals in the engine
Evidence: build/src/normalize/values.js:74-76 turns value +/- uncertainty into {lo,hi,kind:uncertainty}; app/js/engine/constraints.js:43-70 and 140-147 compare lo/hi as hard bounds. M002 PLA Basic tensileStrengthXY 35 +/- 4 MPa is INDETERMINATE for >=33 (mean above threshold) and for >=36. 128 headlines carry an uncertainty interval (Bambu, Polymaker, Fiberlogy sheets), mostly a specimen standard deviation, not a tolerance. The estimate model reads the same half-width as observation noise (estimates.js:281), and impliedBounds reads its top as a bound (compile.js:410, e.g. V002012 30 +/- 23 % becomes 53 %). One number, three meanings.
SuggestedFix: Record what the band is (SD, tolerance, range) or decide one policy in DECISIONS: e.g. judge a measured headline on its value and show the band as a caveat, or treat SD bands as INDETERMINATE only within k*SD. Keep impliedBounds on the value, not value+uncertainty.

Title: Headline selection is not checked for moisture, specimen, post-processing or load
Evidence: build/src/compile.js:295-302 HEADLINE-SELECTION-INVALID checks material, grade, property, unit and direction only. validate.js:219-226 backstops the load (HDT-LOAD-WRONG) and test/database.test.js:468 the moulded case, but nothing refuses a conditioned (moistureState conditioned), film, filament or annealed-when-as-printed-exists selection. Today every headline passes these checks (repro prints only annealed Bambu boilerplate, 6 unstated loads and >-operator bounds), so this is latent; AGENTS.md "Make a measurement a headline" relies on the build to say which rule fails.
SuggestedFix: Extend the compile check: refuse Specimen type Raw material, Film or Filament; refuse moistureState conditioned; for a headline with Load MPa refuse a stated different load at compile time; once C-01 adds a post-processing state, refuse annealed where the same grade and source publish as-printed. Document the new reasons in rules.js.

Title: HDT load parser: both loads resolve to 0.45 silently, psi and kgf/cm2 are ignored, ISO 75 Af/Bf unread
Evidence: build/src/normalize/thermal.js:19-22 and 37-39: the first matching class wins, so "ASTM D648 1.8MPa/0.45MPa" and "ISO 75, 1.8 & 0.45 MPa" read as 0.45; "ASTM D648, 264 psi", "66 psi" and "18.6 kg/cm2" read as load not stated; "ISO 75-2/Af" and "Bf" (flatwise) are not recognised; the unit-less pattern matches inside "ISO 10.45". No current row is wrong: all 195 HDT rows have Test load MPa equal to the parser reading (mapper-table.csv). V002188/V002189 print "ISO 75: Method A (0.45 MPa)" and "Method B (1.80 MPa)" with the letters inverted; the number wins, values are Not published. Because PARSE-MISMATCH compares the typed value with this parser, a wrong parse and a scaffolded typed value would agree.
SuggestedFix: Return loadMPa null with an ambiguity flag when both classes match; add 66/264 psi and 4.6/18.6 kgf/cm2 patterns, Af/Bf/Ae letters, and a leading word boundary on the unit-less number; warn when a method letter contradicts the number.

Title: Estimate calibration is mildly optimistic: spreads, conversions and conflict weights see the hidden headline
Evidence: build/src/estimates.js:571-592 fits conversions (pairs include each headline), the between-product spread fixedW, the empirical-Bayes hyperparameters and the 3.5-sigma conflict down-weighting on all observations; calibration (596-606) and the screening back-test (668-690) then hide only the headline observations by a GP downdate. The downdate itself is exact and the hide set is right for current data: every value headline has kind equal to HEAD (no conditioned, moulded or non-ultimate headline), and no formulation is duplicated across materials (checked by sourceId/property/value). Determinism: no Math.random, Date or unordered iteration in estimates/compile.
SuggestedFix: Document the approximation in DATA-MODEL Estimates, or refit conversions per held-out formulation for the this-grade class (the only class where the hidden headline also calibrates its own conversion pair).

Title: Record-level estimate findings are warnings, so a new one never fails verify
Evidence: build/src/rules.js EST-OUTLIER, EST-WIDE, EST-FAMILY-ORDER and HDT-LOAD-UNSTATED are warn; validate.js:228,294,304,319 aggregate them into one message each. AGENTS.md requires a lint finding to be fixed or accepted with a reason; these per-record findings bypass that, so a fifth outlier or a seventh unstated load reaches dist with no review. Of the 8 current warnings: IMPACT-UNITS (informational, correct), HDT-LOAD-UNSTATED (6: M004 M097 M098 M099 M100 M102, should be per-record accepted findings), EST-SUMMARY and FAMILY-ENTRIES (informational, not warnings), EST-OUTLIER (4: PET-GF is an artefact of C-01; OBC V001683, PPA-CF V001310, PC-ABS V001550 need review), EST-WIDE (14, acceptable with reasons), EST-FAMILY-ORDER (PLA-CF 2.79 < PLA 2.865: different manufacturers, accept), NO-MEASUREMENTS (PA66-CF, PA612-GF, informational).
SuggestedFix: Emit per-record EST-OUTLIER, EST-WIDE, EST-FAMILY-ORDER and HDT-LOAD-UNSTATED as lint findings keyed by record (accepted-findings.csv), and give informational summaries an info level that does not count as a warning.

Title: Rules catalogue and code agree, but compile raises issues without the catalogue check

Title: MEAS-RAW-RECONCILE checks the value but not the upper bound or uncertainty
Evidence: build/src/measurement-rules.js:36-56 reconciles Raw numeric x Conversion factor with Normalized value only. Raw upper bound and Raw uncertainty are converted by hand (e.g. V002204 3368 MPa -> 3.368 GPa, V000380 2600 -> 2.6). SuggestedFix: Apply the same reconciliation to the upper bound and uncertainty pairs, and require both sides of each pair to be numeric or both missing.

Title: Contract: fields written but never read, and headline entries omit post-processing
Evidence: repro/contract.mjs lists db.json keys not mentioned in app/js, among them estimate.screenBasis, estimate.bounds[].side and .sd, related.intervals, materials.measurementConditions, measurements.directionText and grades.formulationKey. related.intervals is written with a comment (compile.js:449-452) saying it stops an estimate screening a material its own measurements could keep; the engine uses impliedBounds instead, so the comment describes a guarantee the field no longer gives. Headline entries (compile.js:309-322) carry direction, specimenType and moisture but not postProcessing, so the table and export cannot show that 119 headlines rest on Bambu Lab sheets worded "annealed and dried at 55-80 C" (133 mention annealing in all) or that the PET-GF HDT headline is as printed while its mechanical headlines are annealed at 120 C. No field is read but never written; loadBracket, impliedBounds, canScreen and screenRange are written and read with matching meaning.
SuggestedFix: Drop related.intervals (or read it) and correct the comment; either surface screenBasis in the drawer or stop writing it; add postProcessing to headline entries.
